items.title: Up First briefing: Thanksgiving weather; Trump tariffs; Iowa; FCC : NPR
items.excerpt: Severe storms sweeping across the nation threaten to cause widespread travel delays today, as millions of people gather with their loved ones. New York City officials announced that the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been rescheduled to Saturday due to the threat of powerful wind gusts that could reach up to 60 mph. This year marked the 100th procession, and the first time the iconic event is being postponed. ... - 🎧 Something is happening across almost every part of the country right now, NPR's Kat Lonsdorf tells Up First. Extreme high tides are affecting the West Coast, snow is expected in parts of the Midwest, and in the South and Southeast, a major storm is advancing up the East Coast. Meteorologist Richard Bann with the National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center tells Lonsdorf the East Coast storm is the primary concern. Bann says the storm will become better organized throughout the day, bringing strong winds and heavy rain that could lead to coastal flooding. The good news: Forecasters expect the East Coast's major storm to move on, mostly wrapping up by Saturday, Lonsdorf says. The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs targeting goods from 14 major U.S. trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union. Administration officials argue the measures counter unfair foreign trade practices, though critics question their ultimate effectiveness. Proposed rates may reach 40% on Chinese imports, 35% on Vietnamese goods, and 20-25% on products from other targeted nations. Additional tariffs on Brazilian sugar and aircraft are also being suggested. ... Federal scientists are testing the air, soil and water in Eastern Iowa for lead contamination after the U.S. Army detonated thousands of pounds of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown yesterday. Officials said the controlled explosion was the only safe way to dispose of the bomb-making compound. - 🎧 Eliza Billingham of NPR network station Iowa Public Radio says the major concern is the potential release of lead into the air from the explosion. She adds that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has tested the area since the detonation and hasn't found lead in the air. The EPA has deployed around 300 people to sample the air, ground and nearby water. Lead is a neurotoxin that especially endangers children and pregnant people because it can impede childhood development. After a week and a half of delays and inconsistent communication from the Army, residents have grown hesitant about the Army and the EPA's initial findings, Billingham says. Residents want independent monitoring and the University of Iowa and the University of Illinois are conducting regional sampling. Results are expected in a few days and should show if their measurements align with the EPA's data, Billingham says.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. "It is more urgent than ever that Fed officials step up the pace of interest rate hikes to cool off economic demand," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "It was once thought that import tariffs and energy prices from the Mideast war were one-off factors behind the higher inflation numbers, but increasingly the inflation fires look to be stoked by old-fashioned economic demand pressures." ... PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. ... items.title: Fed survey shows continued economic growth, sticky inflation in recent weeks By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 25 (Reuters) - Economic growth persisted at a "slight to moderate" pace across most of the US in recent weeks, while inflation remained sticky and employment levels rose, a Federal Reserve survey showed on Wednesday, two weeks before central bank policymakers decide whether to raise interest rates. "Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, health care, insurance, and tariff-related expenses." Still, input costs were outpacing selling price increases, suggesting growing pressure on corporate margins, the report said. "(C)ompetitive pressures and customer price sensitivity limited firms’ ability to fully pass through higher costs. Contacts expected both expenses and prices to continue rising in the coming months." ... The overall picture across the country was varied, with eight districts reporting growth and four reporting that activity was unchanged. Business investment — led by the artificial intelligence boom — remained strong, but consumer spending was flat as households were increasingly stretched and trading down.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate.

Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent). items.title: U.S. tariff-hike threats pile pressure on partners to sign trade deals
items.excerpt: The Trump administration has unveiled a fresh tariff salvo on more than a dozen trading partners, with China, Vietnam, and India facing some of the steepest potential rates and mounting pressure to conclude trade deals with Washington. The proposed tariffs, framed as curbing excess industrial capacity, start at 15% for the European Union, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan and rise to as much as 35% for Vietnam. The U.S. Trade Representative's Office said it intends to cap the new duties at lower levels for countries that have completed trade deals or are still negotiating with Washington. The overall impact on the region is likely to be limited, said Mark Williams, chief Asia economist at Capital Economics. The proposal "puts most of the targeted countries back where they were earlier in the year," he said, after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's emergency tariffs in February. Still, the proposal could give some countries an incentive to speed up trade talks in order to lock in lower tariff rates, analysts said. On Wednesday, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that the new policy likely will not take effect for months, with a senior U.S. official saying the duties could take effect as early as January.

Bollywood union asks Modi to bar Netflix's Pakistani series in India A prominent Bollywood workers' union has asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to ban a forthcoming Pakistani series on Netflix in India, while ⁠seeking a law prohibiting ​content from its foe from being shown in the country. The first ⁠part of "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" (All the Love Our Hearts Carry) is scheduled to air on Netflix on December 4 and is the global streaming giant's first Urdu-language series. Several top Pakistani actors feature in it. Top Gear to return in 2028 with celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay as lead host British celebrity chef and television presenter ⁠Gordon Ramsay will host a revived version of the BBC's long-running motoring show "Top Gear" when it returns to screens in 2028, the broadcaster said on Wednesday. Produced by BBC Studios, the new series will be filmed in 2027 and feature a new lineup of co-presenters alongside Ramsay, while the programme's test driver, ​The Stig, will also return, the BBC said. Paralympics-Ezra Frech's Mirrorball win builds buzz for LA28 Paralympics US Paralympian Ezra Frech's victory on "Dancing with the Stars" could help reshape perceptions of disability and build interest in the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics, fellow ⁠athletes and organizers said after the 21-year-old won the show's coveted Mirrorball trophy on Tuesday. Frech and professional partner Daniella Karagach won the 35th season of the televised dance competition after receiving perfect scores for each of their three finale routines. More than 86 million votes were cast during the three-hour finale, according to the show. Tarantino-Fincher collaboration 'Cliff Booth' ⁠came ​with pressure and fun, cast say Brad Pitt reunites with Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher to bring another eventful episode of stuntman Cliff Booth's life to the screen. Pitt won an Oscar for his portrayal of the laid-back stunt double in Tarantino's 2019 "Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood" and worked with Fincher on films including "Fight Club" and "Se7en."
